content_of_post_to_answer: Is silence the mind at rest, or the mind finally heard?
answer: Silence is not always the absence of noise; sometimes it is the moment when distractions stop drowning out what was already there. A restless mind often fears silence because it finally encounters its own unresolved thoughts. But a settled mind experiences the same silence differently: not as emptiness, but as clarity. The difference is not in the silence itself, but in our relationship with what appears when everything else disappears.
